Simonds d'Ewes.question: He died on 18 April _____, having married again, to Elizabeth Willoughby, daughter of Sir Henry Willoughby, 1st Baronet of Risley, Derbyshire and his first wife Elizabeth Knollys, daughter of Sir Henr
Simonds d'Ewes.fact: He died on 18 April 1650, having married again, to Elizabeth Willoughby, daughter of Sir Henry Willoughby, 1st Baronet of Risley, Derbyshire and his first wife Elizabeth Knollys, daughter of Sir Henry Knollys.

Simonds d'Ewes.subject: Computer & IT
Simonds d'Ewes.question: By Elizabeth, he had his second and only surviving son and heir, _____, who succeeded as second baronet
Simonds d'Ewes.fact: He died on 18 April 1650, having married again, to Elizabeth Willoughby, daughter of Sir Henry Willoughby, 1st Baronet of Risley, Derbyshire and his first wife Elizabeth Knollys, daughter of Sir Henry Knollys. Simonds d'Ewes.question: The Journals were published posthumously in _____ by his nephew, the lawyer and antiquary Paul Bowes

Simonds d'Ewes.fact: The Library of Sir Simonds d’Ewes is a detailed examination that reflects on the early history of books in England as manifested in d'Ewes' collection.

Simonds d'Ewes.question: He also kept a diary, which gives an insight into the events in _____, as well as glimpses of his own character

Simonds d'Ewes.question: Of the events leading to the abrupt dissolution of Parliament in March _____, he wrote that "diverse fiery spirits in the House of Commons were very faulty and cannot be excused"

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: What do you know about Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP)?
Simple Network Management Protocol.answer: an Internet Standard protocol for collecting and organizing information about managed devices on IP networks and for mod
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) is an Internet Standard protocol for collecting and organizing information about managed devices on IP networks and for modifying that information to change device behavior.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: Devices that typically support _____ include cable modems, routers, network switches, servers, workstations, printers, and more
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) is an Internet Standard protocol for collecting and organizing information about managed devices on IP networks and for modifying that information to change device behavior. Devices that typically support SNMP include cable modems, routers, network switches, servers, workstations, printers, and more.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: Three significant versions of _____ have been developed and deployed
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: SNMP is widely used in network management for network monitoring. SNMP exposes management data in the form of variables on the managed systems organized in a management information base (MIB), which describes the system status and configuration.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: SNMP is a component of the _____ as defined by the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF)
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: SNMP is a component of the Internet Protocol Suite as defined by the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF).

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: Each managed system executes a software component called an agent that reports information via _____ to the manager
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: More recent versions, SNMPv2c and SNMPv3, feature improvements in performance, flexibility and security. SNMP is a component of the Internet Protocol Suite as defined by the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF).

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: An agent has local knowledge of management information and translates that information to or from an _____-specific form
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: An agent has local knowledge of management information and translates that information to or from an SNMP-specific form.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: The variables accessible via _____ are organized in hierarchies
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: The variables accessible via SNMP are organized in hierarchies. SNMP itself does not define which variables a managed system should offer.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: Rather, _____ uses an extensible design that allows applications to define their own hierarchies
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: The variables accessible via SNMP are organized in hierarchies. SNMP itself does not define which variables a managed system should offer.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: Each OID identifies a variable that can be read or set via _____
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: Rather, SNMP uses an extensible design that allows applications to define their own hierarchies. Each OID identifies a variable that can be read or set via SNMP.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: MIBs use the notation defined by Structure of _____ 2.0 (SMIv2, RFC 2578), a subset of ASN.1
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: MIBs use the notation defined by Structure of Management Information Version 2.0 (SMIv2, RFC 2578), a subset of ASN.1.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: All SNMP messages are transported via _____ (UDP)
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: All SNMP messages are transported via User Datagram Protocol (UDP).

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: The _____ agent receives requests on UDP port 161
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: Each OID identifies a variable that can be read or set via SNMP. All SNMP messages are transported via User Datagram Protocol (UDP).

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: The manager receives notifications (Traps and Inform_____) on port 162
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: The SNMP agent receives requests on UDP port 161. The manager may send requests from any available source port to port 161 in the agent.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: When used with _____ or Datagram Transport Layer Security, requests are received on port 10161 and notifications are sent to port 10162
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: When used with Transport Layer Security or Datagram Transport Layer Security, requests are received on port 10161 and notifications are sent to port 10162.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: Two other PDUs, GetBulk_____ and InformRequest were added in SNMPv2 and the Report PDU was added in SNMPv3
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: When used with Transport Layer Security or Datagram Transport Layer Security, requests are received on port 10161 and notifications are sent to port 10162. Two other PDUs, GetBulkRequest and InformRequest were added in SNMPv2 and the Report PDU was added in SNMPv3.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: A _____ with current values is returned
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: A Response with current values is returned.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: Set_____ A manager-to-agent request to change the value of a variable or list of variables
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: SetRequest A manager-to-agent request to change the value of a variable or list of variables. Variable bindings are specified in the body of the request.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: A _____ with (current) new values for the variables is returned
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: A Response with (current) new values for the variables is returned. Returns a Response with variable binding for the lexicographically next variable in the MIB.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: Returns a _____ with variable binding for the lexicographically next variable in the MIB
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: A Response with (current) new values for the variables is returned. Returns a Response with variable binding for the lexicographically next variable in the MIB.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: GetNext_____ A manager-to-agent request to discover available variables and their values
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: Variable bindings are specified in the body of the request. GetNextRequest A manager-to-agent request to discover available variables and their values.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: The entire MIB of an agent can be walked by iterative application of _____ starting at OID 0
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: GetNextRequest A manager-to-agent request to discover available variables and their values. The entire MIB of an agent can be walked by iterative application of GetNextRequest starting at OID 0.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: GetBulk_____ A manager-to-agent request for multiple iterations of GetNextRequest
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: The entire MIB of an agent can be walked by iterative application of GetNextRequest starting at OID 0. Rows of a table can be read by specifying column OIDs in the variable bindings of the request.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: An optimized version of _____
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: The entire MIB of an agent can be walked by iterative application of GetNextRequest starting at OID 0. GetBulkRequest A manager-to-agent request for multiple iterations of GetNextRequest.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: Returns a _____ with multiple variable bindings walked from the variable binding or bindings in the request
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: Returns a Response with multiple variable bindings walked from the variable binding or bindings in the request. PDU specific non-repeaters and max-repetitions fields are used to control response behavior.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: GetBulk_____ was introduced in SNMPv2
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: An optimized version of GetNextRequest. Returns a Response with multiple variable bindings walked from the variable binding or bindings in the request.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: Response Returns variable bindings and acknowledgement from agent to manager for Get_____, SetRequest, GetNextRequest, GetBulkRequest and InformRequest
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: Returns a Response with multiple variable bindings walked from the variable binding or bindings in the request. GetBulkRequest was introduced in SNMPv2.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: Although it was used as a response to both gets and sets, this PDU was called Get_____ in SNMPv1
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: Response Returns variable bindings and acknowledgement from agent to manager for GetRequest, SetRequest, GetNextRequest, GetBulkRequest and InformRequest. Although it was used as a response to both gets and sets, this PDU was called GetResponse in SNMPv1.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: While in other _____ communication, the manager actively requests information from the agent, these are PDUs that are sent from the agent to the manager without being explicitly requested
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: Although it was used as a response to both gets and sets, this PDU was called GetResponse in SNMPv1. While in other SNMP communication, the manager actively requests information from the agent, these are PDUs that are sent from the agent to the manager without being explicitly requested.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: SNMP _____ enable an agent to notify the management station of significant events by way of an unsolicited SNMP message
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: SNMP Traps enable an agent to notify the management station of significant events by way of an unsolicited SNMP message. Destination addressing for traps is determined in an application-specific manner, typically through trap configuration variables in the MIB.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: Trap PDUs include current sysUp_____ value, an OID identifying the type of trap and optional variable bindings
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: Trap PDUs include current sysUpTime value, an OID identifying the type of trap and optional variable bindings.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: The format of the trap message was changed in _____2 and the PDU was renamed SNMPv2-Trap
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: The format of the trap message was changed in SNMPv2 and the PDU was renamed SNMPv2-Trap. This PDU was introduced in SNMPv2 and was originally defined as manager to manager communication.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: This PDU was introduced in _____2 and was originally defined as manager to manager communication
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: The format of the trap message was changed in SNMPv2 and the PDU was renamed SNMPv2-Trap. This PDU was introduced in SNMPv2 and was originally defined as manager to manager communication.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: Inform_____ asynchronous notification
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: InformRequest Acknowledged asynchronous notification.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: Inform_____ fixes this as an acknowledgement is returned on receipt
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: InformRequest fixes this as an acknowledgement is returned on receipt. If implemented correctly, an SNMP message is discarded if the decoding of the message fails and thus malformed SNMP requests are ignored.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT

Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: RFC 1157 specifies that an SNMP implementation must accept a message of at least 484 bytes in length.

Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: Manager-to-manager notifications were already possible in SNMPv1 using a Trap, but as SNMP commonly runs over UDP where delivery is not assured and dropped packets are not reported, delivery of a Trap was not guaranteed. RFC 1157 specifies that an SNMP implementation must accept a message of at least 484 bytes in length.

Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: Manager-to-manager notifications were already possible in SNMPv1 using a Trap, but as SNMP commonly runs over UDP where delivery is not assured and dropped packets are not reported, delivery of a Trap was not guaranteed. RFC 1157 specifies that an SNMP implementation must accept a message of at least 484 bytes in length.

Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: RFC 1157 specifies that an SNMP implementation must accept a message of at least 484 bytes in length. In practice, SNMP implementations accept longer messages.

Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: SNMPv1 may be carried by transport layer protocols such as User Datagram Protocol (UDP), OSI Connectionless-mode Network Service (CLNS), AppleTalk Datagram Delivery Protocol (DDP), and Novell Internetwork Packet Exchange (IPX). The specification does, in fact, allow room for custom authentication to be used, but widely used implementations "support only a trivial authentication service that identifies all SNMP messages as authentic SNMP messages." The security of the messages, therefore, beco...

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: It introduced GetBulk_____, an alternative to iterative GetNextRequests for retrieving large amounts of management data in a single request
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: It introduced GetBulkRequest, an alternative to iterative GetNextRequests for retrieving large amounts of management data in a single request.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: The new party-based security system introduced in _____2, viewed by many as overly complex, was not widely adopted
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: The new party-based security system introduced in SNMPv2, viewed by many as overly complex, was not widely adopted. Community-Based Simple Network Management Protocol version 2, or SNMPv2c, is defined in RFC 1901–RFC 1908.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: This version of SNMP reached the _____ level of maturity, but was deemed obsolete by later versions
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: This version of SNMP reached the Proposed Standard level of maturity, but was deemed obsolete by later versions.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: Community-Based Simple Network Management Protocol version 2, or SNMPv2c, is defined in RFC _____–RFC 1908
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: Community-Based Simple Network Management Protocol version 2, or SNMPv2c, is defined in RFC 1901–RFC 1908.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: This version is one of relatively few standards to meet the IETF's _____ maturity level, and was widely considered the de facto SNMPv2 standard
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: This version is one of relatively few standards to meet the IETF's Draft Standard maturity level, and was widely considered the de facto SNMPv2 standard.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: It was later restated as part of _____3
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: Community-Based Simple Network Management Protocol version 2, or SNMPv2c, is defined in RFC 1901–RFC 1908. SNMPv2c comprises SNMPv2 without the controversial new SNMP v2 security model, using instead the simple community-based security scheme of SNMPv1.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: User-Based Simple Network Management Protocol version 2, or SNMPv2u, is defined in RFC _____–RFC 1910
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: User-Based Simple Network Management Protocol version 2, or SNMPv2u, is defined in RFC 1909–RFC 1910.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: This is a compromise that attempts to offer greater security than _____1, but without incurring the high complexity of SNMPv2
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: This version is one of relatively few standards to meet the IETF's Draft Standard maturity level, and was widely considered the de facto SNMPv2 standard. It was later restated as part of SNMPv3.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: A variant of this was commercialized as _____ v2*, and the mechanism was eventually adopted as one of two security frameworks in SNMP v3
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: It was later restated as part of SNMPv3. User-Based Simple Network Management Protocol version 2, or SNMPv2u, is defined in RFC 1909–RFC 1910.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: Version 1 was designed only with 32-bit counters, which can store integer values from zero to _____ (precisely 4294967295)
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: Version 1 was designed only with 32-bit counters, which can store integer values from zero to 4.29 billion (precisely 4294967295).

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: A _____-bit version 1 counter cannot store the maximum speed of a 10-gigabit or larger interface, expressed in bits per second
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: Version 1 was designed only with 32-bit counters, which can store integer values from zero to 4.29 billion (precisely 4294967295). A 32-bit version 1 counter cannot store the maximum speed of a 10-gigabit or larger interface, expressed in bits per second.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: For example, 1.6 terabit Ethernet is predicted to become available by _____
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: For example, 1.6 terabit Ethernet is predicted to become available by 2025.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: A 64-bit counter incrementing at a rate of _____ bits per second would be able to retain information for such an interface without rolling over for 133 days
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: A 64-bit counter incrementing at a rate of 1.6 trillion bits per second would be able to retain information for such an interface without rolling over for 133 days.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: Get_____ messages are converted by the proxy agent to GetNext messages and then are forwarded to the SNMPv1 agent
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: GetBulk messages are converted by the proxy agent to GetNext messages and then are forwarded to the SNMPv1 agent.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: Based on the information in the database, the NMS communicates with the agent using the appropriate version of _____
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: GetBulk messages are converted by the proxy agent to GetNext messages and then are forwarded to the SNMPv1 agent. Additionally, the proxy agent receives and maps SNMPv1 trap messages to SNMPv2 trap messages and then forwards them to the NMS.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: The most visible change was to define a secure version of _____, by adding security and remote configuration enhancements to SNMP
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: Additionally, the proxy agent receives and maps SNMPv1 trap messages to SNMPv2 trap messages and then forwards them to the NMS. To support this dual-management environment, a management application examines information stored in a local database to determine whether the agent supports SNMPv1 or SNMPv2.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: The changes also facilitate remote configuration and administration of the _____ entities, as well as addressing issues related to the large-scale deployment, accounting, and fault management
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: The most visible change was to define a secure version of SNMP, by adding security and remote configuration enhancements to SNMP. For the administration aspect, SNMPv3 focuses on two parts, namely notification originators and proxy forwarders.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: Traps and _____ are exceptions to this rule
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: Traps and Notifications are exceptions to this rule.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: Masquerade – _____ against attempting management operations not authorized for some principal by assuming the identity of another principal that has the appropriate authorizations
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: Definition of security goals where the goals of message authentication service include protection against the following: Modification of Information – Protection against some unauthorized SNMP entity altering in-transit messages generated by an authorized principal. Masquerade – Protection against attempting management operations not authorized for some principal by assuming the identity of another principal that has the appropriate authorizations.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: Message stream modification – _____ against messages getting maliciously re-ordered, delayed, or replayed to affect unauthorized management operations
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: Definition of security goals where the goals of message authentication service include protection against the following: Modification of Information – Protection against some unauthorized SNMP entity altering in-transit messages generated by an authorized principal. Masquerade – Protection against attempting management operations not authorized for some principal by assuming the identity of another principal that has the appropriate authorizations.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: Disclosure – _____ against eavesdropping on the exchanges between SNMP engines
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: Definition of security goals where the goals of message authentication service include protection against the following: Modification of Information – Protection against some unauthorized SNMP entity altering in-transit messages generated by an authorized principal. Masquerade – Protection against attempting management operations not authorized for some principal by assuming the identity of another principal that has the appropriate authorizations.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: Specification for USM – USM consists of the general definition of the following communication mechanisms available: _____ without authentication and privacy (NoAuthNoPriv)
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: Specification for USM – USM consists of the general definition of the following communication mechanisms available: Communication without authentication and privacy (NoAuthNoPriv). Communication with authentication and without privacy (AuthNoPriv).

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: Communication with authentication and without privacy (_____NoPriv)
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: Message stream modification – Protection against messages getting maliciously re-ordered, delayed, or replayed to affect unauthorized management operations. Specification for USM – USM consists of the general definition of the following communication mechanisms available: Communication without authentication and privacy (NoAuthNoPriv).

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: Definition of different authentication and privacy protocols – MD5, SHA and _____-SHA-2 authentication protocols and the CBC_DES and CFB_AES_128 privacy protocols are supported in the USM
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: Definition of different authentication and privacy protocols – MD5, SHA and HMAC-SHA-2 authentication protocols and the CBC_DES and CFB_AES_128 privacy protocols are supported in the USM.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: Definition of a discovery procedure – To find the SNMP_____ID of an SNMP entity for a given transport address and transport endpoint address
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: Definition of a discovery procedure – To find the SNMPEngineID of an SNMP entity for a given transport address and transport endpoint address.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: Definition of the time synchronization procedure – To facilitate authenticated communication between the _____ entities
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: Definition of a discovery procedure – To find the SNMPEngineID of an SNMP entity for a given transport address and transport endpoint address. Definition of the time synchronization procedure – To facilitate authenticated communication between the SNMP entities.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: Definition of the _____ framework MIB – To facilitate remote configuration and administration of the SNMP entity
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: Definition of a discovery procedure – To find the SNMPEngineID of an SNMP entity for a given transport address and transport endpoint address. Definition of the time synchronization procedure – To facilitate authenticated communication between the SNMP entities.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: Definition of the view-based access control model (_____) MIBs – To facilitate remote configuration and administration of the access control module
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: Definition of the view-based access control model (VACM) MIBs – To facilitate remote configuration and administration of the access control module.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: Security was one of the biggest weaknesses of _____ until v3
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: Definition of the SNMP framework MIB – To facilitate remote configuration and administration of the SNMP entity. Security was one of the biggest weaknesses of SNMP until v3.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: Authentication in _____ 1 and 2 amounts to nothing more than a password (community string) sent in clear text between a manager and agent
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: Authentication in SNMP Versions 1 and 2 amounts to nothing more than a password (community string) sent in clear text between a manager and agent.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: The security approach in v3 targets: _____ – Encryption of packets to prevent snooping by an unauthorized source
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: The security approach in v3 targets: Confidentiality – Encryption of packets to prevent snooping by an unauthorized source.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: Integrity – _____ integrity to ensure that a packet has not been tampered with while in transit, including an optional packet replay protection mechanism
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: Each SNMPv3 message contains security parameters that are encoded as an octet string. Integrity – Message integrity to ensure that a packet has not been tampered with while in transit, including an optional packet replay protection mechanism.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: v3 also defines the USM and _____, which were later followed by a transport security model (TSM) that provided support for SNMPv3 over SSH and SNMPv3 over TLS and DTLS
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: v3 also defines the USM and VACM, which were later followed by a transport security model (TSM) that provided support for SNMPv3 over SSH and SNMPv3 over TLS and DTLS. VACM (View-based Access Control Model) determines whether a given principal is allowed access to a particular MIB object to perform specific functions and operates at the PDU level.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: USM (User-based _____) provides authentication and privacy (encryption) functions and operates at the message level
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: v3 also defines the USM and VACM, which were later followed by a transport security model (TSM) that provided support for SNMPv3 over SSH and SNMPv3 over TLS and DTLS. USM (User-based Security Model) provides authentication and privacy (encryption) functions and operates at the message level.

Simple Network Management Protocol.subject: Computer & IT
Simple Network Management Protocol.question: VACM (View-based _____) determines whether a given principal is allowed access to a particular MIB object to perform specific functions and operates at the PDU level
Simple Network Management Protocol.fact: VACM (View-based Access Control Model) determines whether a given principal is allowed access to a particular MIB object to perform specific functions and operates at the PDU level.
